impact: Ground zero. Globally popularized conversational generative AI and kicked off the modern competitive cycle.
First major leap post-ChatGPT: strong advance in reasoning, initial multimodality, and high-level benchmarks.
Consolidated the axis of "more context + lower cost + dev ecosystem", accelerating adoption in product and API.
Not a broad product launch; entered as an announcement that signaled a paradigm shift in text→video.
Shift to native real-time multimodality, unifying text, vision, and voice in a single system.
Explicit start of the reasoning models phase, with OpenAI positioning the new series as models that "think" before answering.
Showed that strong reasoning could move down to a faster and cheaper tier, increasing competitive pressure.
Research preview that normalized the idea of delegating long engineering tasks to agents within ChatGPT.
Unified system with built-in thinking; broad leap in multimodal capability, coding, tool use, and professional use.
Refined GPT-5 generation with smarter, more conversational responses, and better reasoning calibration.
Model aimed at professional work, with a strong advance in coding, computer use, tool-based search, and complex workflows.
New generation of image generation integrated into ChatGPT and APIs.
Agentic model focused on workflows with tools, research, and complex code.
First major commercial alternative born from the same technical-cultural core, competing for the frontier with OpenAI.
Put Anthropic back at the top of the benchmark race and increased competitive pressure on GPT-4 and Gemini.
Became the reference for balancing quality, speed, and code; one of the most influential models of 2024.
Anthropic introduced it as the market's first hybrid reasoning model.
Transformed the model into a programming execution environment, helping to popularize the "model as coder" workflow.
Consolidation of Anthropic in agentic coding, computer use, and long-duration complex tasks.
Updated version with superior reasoning and agentic execution capabilities.
Google's structural response, born as a multimodal family already integrated into its ecosystem.
Milestone of the "agentic era" in Google's discourse and product, with multimodality, native output, and tool use.
Positioned by Google as its smartest model to date, with a strong emphasis on reasoning.
New generation of Gemini with a leap in reasoning, multimodality, and practical use in products and development.
Google's formal entry into the IDE and agent-first development environments war.
Important reasoning upgrade for complex tasks, with an emphasis on agentic workflows and hard benchmarks.
Evolution of Google's family of open and computationally efficient models, consolidating the "on-device" option.
Milestone of the modern open-weight model cycle in the West; shifted the race beyond fully closed systems.
New leap for Meta's open models, bringing open-weight closer to capabilities previously associated with closed systems.
New visual generation model focused on creativity and performance.
Start of NVIDIA's model family for enterprise workflows.
Massive launch focused on synthetic data generation and fine-tuning.
Open-weight omni-modal model created for agent workflows.
General availability of Background Agent and BugBot; moved AI coding from autocomplete to delegated workflow.
Explosion of open and self-hosted agents: a sign that autonomous execution left the chat and became user infrastructure.
Initial verifiable milestone of the Qwen line and Alibaba's consistent open-weight trajectory.
Instructional refinement of an open-weight model with expanded capabilities.
Consolidated Alibaba among the strongest open families, with heavy cross-border developer use.
New generation with hybrid reasoning; reinforced Chinese strength in open-weight.
Significant advance in the open Qwen line, strengthening multilingual and coding capabilities.
Preview of generation 3.6 with an advanced focus on reasoning and agentic AI.
Introduced a cheeky model with real-time data access in the X ecosystem.
Point improvements in reasoning, coding, and introduction of long context.
Introduction of vision capabilities (multimodality) to the Grok family.
Frontier-class launch with strong performance and image generation integration.
Strong leap in reasoning and scale, aggressively challenging the top of global benchmarks.
Iterative update with native multimodality in videos.
First major visible Chinese response to the cycle inaugurated by ChatGPT.
Point of aggressive ascent for DeepSeek on the cost/capability axis and MoE architecture.
The late 2024 shock, challenging American SOTA systems with hyper-efficient training and usage.
One of the most important launches on the Chinese ruler: an open reasoning model with enormous global repercussion.
Refined evolution with agentic coupling for the local Chinese ecosystem.
Massive evolution challenging premium Western models with very high computational efficiency.
First major launch of the M series, establishing the foundation for new multimodals.
Launch of the M2.5 series and the M2.5-Lightning variant.
Multimodal flagship launched as part of the M series, with competitive global capabilities.
Generational leap that put Zhipu AI on the level of GPT-4 in several global benchmarks.
Refinement of line 4 with significant improvements and preparation for the fifth generation.
Launch of the new generation with a revamped architecture and performance leap.
Updated version of series 5, released in open source.
Initial launch with a huge context window (128K), popularizing the use of "long context".
First major evolution of the series, expanding reasoning capabilities.
Introduction of Agent Swarm and native multimodal capabilities in the K2 line.
Flagship launched with a focus on deep reasoning and operational agents.
Ground zero. Globally popularized conversational generative AI and kicked off the modern competitive cycle.
Introduction of highly efficient compact models with conditional reasoning ("toggleable reasoning") and vision models specialized in documents.
Launch of an open-source family based on a hybrid Mamba/Transformer architecture, reducing RAM consumption by over 70% for long contexts.
Massive intelligence and reliability upgrade with RL training, enabling complex autonomous tasks at a tenth of the cost of frontier models.
Evolution of the Flash series designed for high performance in code and multi-agent flows with excellent cost-benefit, surpassing the intelligence of version 3.1 Pro.
Transformation of the ecosystem into an independent platform optimized for multi-agent development, bringing the new SDK and integration with Gemini 3.5 Flash.
Top-tier proprietary model optimized for the agent era. Features 1M token context, Extended-Thinking, and high performance in long-term reasoning, complex coding, and workflow automation.

Open-weights model family (Apache 2.0 license) with 3B, 8B, and 30B parameters. Highly efficient, focused on tool calling, instructions, and coding, supporting a native 131K context window extendable up to 512K.

New generation of Anthropic's top-tier model, with improvements in agentic coding (69.2%), manual control of effort level, a 2.5x faster quick mode, and integration with dynamic workflows in Claude Code.
Lightweight sparse architecture open-weight model of very high speed for everyday tasks in the Xiaomi device ecosystem.
Xiaomi's proprietary reasoning flagship with over 1T parameters and 1M context, focused on complex agents and tested under the codename Hunter Alpha.
1.02T parameter MoE (42B active), 1M token context, open source (MIT), leader in agentic benchmarks and software engineering.

Proprietary agentic multimodal model with 1M context, accepting text, image, and video. Unifies GUI and CLI operation in a single agent, allowing interface navigation, screen interpretation, and coding from visual references — at ~10× lower cost than Max.

MiniMax's next-generation multimodal flagship, with MSA (MiniMax Sparse Attention) architecture and 1M token context. Trained from scratch on interleaved multimedia data (text, image, video). Reports 59% on SWE-Bench Pro, surpassing GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro in agentic coding.

NVIDIA's open-weight flagship with 550B total parameters (55B active), hybrid Mamba-2 + Transformer architecture with LatentMoE. 1M token context, focused on frontier reasoning and complex agents. Positioned as the most capable open-weights model developed in the US.

Anthropic's Mythos-class model for general use, with safety classifiers. 1M token window, 128k output. Designed for software engineering and long-horizon tasks. Suspended on Jun/12 by US export control directive.
DeepMind's experimental open-weight model. Uses discrete diffusion instead of autoregressive decoding. Up to 4× faster in text generation on dedicated GPUs.

Open-weight model (modified MIT) for agentic coding. MoE architecture with ~1T total parameters (32B active). +21.8% on Kimi Code Bench v2. ~30% reduction in thinking-tokens usage vs K2.6. 262K token window.
Zhipu AI (Z.ai) MoE model for long-horizon coding and long document processing. 1M token window (5× larger than GLM-5.1). Open-source under MIT license.

Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5, the most agentic Sonnet model yet, with relevant gains in reasoning, tool use, and coding over Sonnet 4.6. It became the default model in the Free and Pro plans, with performance close to Opus 4.8 at a much lower cost.

Mistral AI's first model, a 7 billion parameter open LLM under the Apache 2.0 license. Surpassed Llama 2 13B on all evaluated benchmarks, putting the French startup on the open-source AI map just months after its founding.

Open sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model that activates only ~13B of 47B parameters per token. Matched or surpassed GPT-3.5 and Llama 2 70B on most benchmarks with much more efficient inference, popularizing the MoE architecture in the open ecosystem.

Frontier model with 123B parameters and open weights (research license), with a 128k token context window and strong performance in code, math, and multilingual reasoning. Narrowed the gap to GPT-4o and Llama 3.1 405B.

Mistral's first reasoning models, in Magistral Small (open) and Magistral Medium (proprietary) versions, with explicit chain of thought and multilingual transparency in reasoning. Marked the company's entry into the reasoning models category.

Open model that unifies three previously separate lines into one product — Magistral (reasoning), Pixtral (multimodal vision), and Devstral (agentic code) — simplifying the company's portfolio into a compact and multimodal model.
First model of the Phi family (1.3B parameters). Introduced the "Textbooks Are All You Need" thesis: very high-quality data allows small models to rival giants in code.
2.7B parameter SLM that matches or surpasses models up to 25× larger in reasoning, math, and code — a milestone for "small language models".
3.8B SLM capable of running locally on a smartphone, with performance comparable to GPT-3.5. Consolidated Microsoft's "on-device" AI strategy.
Open family (mini, MoE, and vision) that expanded Phi to multimodality and Mixture-of-Experts, outperforming similarly sized competitors from Google and OpenAI.
14B SLM focused on complex reasoning and math, outperforming much larger models; launched in preview on Azure AI Foundry.
Small models fine-tuned for reasoning (reasoning, reasoning-plus, and mini-reasoning) that outperform larger models on logic and math benchmarks.

xAI (currently also referred to as SpaceXAI) launched Grok 4.5, its first model trained jointly with Cursor, focused on coding and agentic tasks. Elon Musk described the model as "Opus-class", but faster and cheaper, priced at $2/$6 per million tokens (input/output) with a 500 thousand token context window.

Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3, a native multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 2.8 trillion parameters and a 1 million token context window, built on the Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals architectures. The model ranked 1st on the Frontend Code Arena and near the top of several leaderboards, surpassing Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 on its own benchmarks, behind only Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. Full weights will be released by 07/27/2026, but the API has been available since the announcement.

Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5, successor to Opus 4.8, with state-of-the-art in agentic coding benchmarks (Frontier-Bench, GDPval-AA), a 1M token context window, and up to 128K output tokens. The model became the default for Claude Max and the strongest available in Claude Pro, maintaining the price of $5/$25 per million tokens.

DeepSeek launched the official version of V4-Flash (284B total parameters, 13B active, MoE) in public beta, with performance close to Claude Opus 4.8 on coding and agent tasks (Terminal-Bench 2.1: 82.7; SWE-bench Verified: 54.4). API cost is about 99% lower than Opus 4.8.

Alibaba's largest and most capable model to date: 2.4 trillion parameters in a sparse MoE architecture with hybrid attention, 1M token context, and multimodal input (text, image, and video). Aimed at autonomous programming and long-horizon tasks; on benchmarks released by the company itself, it scores 86.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 92.6 on GPQA Diamond, comparable to Claude Fable 5. Available via API on Model Studio and QwenWork at $2/$6 per million input/output tokens, with open weights promised for the following week — alongside Qwen3.8-27B, the first time Alibaba opens a Max-class model.
Pushed reasoning with tools and vision forward at the same time, reinforcing the narrative of agents that act. Announced alongside o4-mini.
Pushed reasoning with tools and vision forward at the same time, reinforcing the narrative of agents that act. Announced alongside o3.
Important shift by Anthropic towards coding, advanced reasoning, and agents. Announced alongside Claude 4 Sonnet.
Important shift by Anthropic towards coding, advanced reasoning, and agents. Announced alongside Claude 4 Opus.
Cursor went from AI IDE to multi-agent interface, reinforcing the agent-first thesis. Launched alongside Composer, its first proprietary coding model.
Cursor's first proprietary coding model, launched with Cursor 2.0 — the transition from AI IDE to multi-agent interface.

Top of the GPT-5.6 family: frontier reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, with a new maximum reasoning mode and an "ultra mode" that uses subagents. Initial access limited to about 20 partners approved by the US government.
Balanced model of the GPT-5.6 family, for everyday use. Announced alongside Sol and Luna, with a new maximum reasoning mode and an "ultra mode" that uses subagents.
Fast and economical model of the GPT-5.6 family. Announced alongside Sol and Terra, with a new maximum reasoning mode and an "ultra mode" that uses subagents.
Multi-agent orchestration model that dynamically selects and coordinates frontier models (proprietary and third-party) via a single API compatible with OpenAI's.

Top version of Fugu. According to Sakana AI, it matches models like Claude Fable 5 and Mythos Preview in engineering, science, and reasoning benchmarks, surpassing GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Opus 4.8 in 10 of 11 disclosed benchmarks.
Sparse MoE with 41B active parameters (675B total). New frontier open generation, which brought Mistral closer to the largest labs while maintaining the bet on open weights.
Three dense models (3B, 8B, and 14B) from Mistral's new open generation, announced alongside Mistral Large 3.
First multimodal Phi (5.6B), unifying speech, vision, and text in a single architecture and leader of the OpenASR ranking.
Compact 3.8B model with 128k context, announced alongside Phi-4-multimodal.
Microsoft AI's first proprietary foundation model (outside of OpenAI): text, trained on about 15 thousand H100 GPUs.
Microsoft AI's proprietary high-fidelity voice model: 1 minute of audio in less than 1 second. Announced alongside MAI-1-preview.
Expansion of the proprietary MAI family in Microsoft Foundry to image, reducing OpenAI dependency.
Proprietary speech transcription model (25 languages) in Microsoft Foundry, announced alongside MAI-Image-2.
At Build 2026, Microsoft's first "flagship" reasoning model, comparable to Claude Opus 4.6 in code.
Microsoft's code model integrated into GitHub Copilot and VS Code, announced at Build 2026 alongside MAI-Thinking-1.
New general-purpose model of the Flash line, with better performance in code and multimodality and 17% fewer output tokens than 3.5 Flash.
Aimed at high throughput and low latency tasks, with built-in computer use.
Fine-tuned for vulnerability detection and correction, with restricted access for governments and partners via the CodeMender program.
New generation of Grok, presented in a livestream, with first-principles reasoning, native tool use, and real-time search. Accompanied by Grok 4 Heavy, a multi-agent variant for complex problems.

1 trillion parameter MoE (32B active) with open weights under a modified MIT license. State-of-the-art among non-thinking models in frontier knowledge, math, and code — and the most talked-about open-weights model of the year.
Native agentic LLM that unified reasoning, code, and agent behavior in a single model, open-sourced under MIT. Launched alongside Zhipu's rebrand to Z.ai in the international market.
OpenAI's first open-weight models since GPT-2, under the Apache 2.0 license. gpt-oss-120b approaches o4-mini in reasoning running on a single 80 GB GPU; gpt-oss-20b runs on devices with 16 GB.
Announced as "the best code model in the world", with a leap in agent building and computer use, plus gains in reasoning and math.
Z.ai's top code model, with context window expanded from 128K to 200K tokens and gains in real programming. Open under MIT.
Reasoning version of K2, with open weights: a "thinking agent" trained to interleave chain of thought with tool calls, planning, acting, and self-correcting.
Announced as the best model in the world for code, agents, and computer use, with a significant price drop compared to previous Opus models ($5/$25 per million tokens).
Successor to GPT-5.1 in the main ChatGPT line, with intelligence and productivity gains. Available in the API in two configurations: GPT-5.2 Thinking and GPT-5.2 Instant.
OpenAI's most capable agentic code model to date, optimized for long-horizon work and large codebase changes.
Most capable Sonnet yet, with advances in code, computer use, long-context reasoning, agent planning, and design.

First Korean model to reach the global top: 314B parameter MoE (13B active per token) and native 262K token context, with proprietary attention (GDLA) and activation (polynorm) mechanisms. Open weights, but with a license restricted to personal, educational, and non-commercial research use. Built by a subsidiary of chipmaker Moreh, with about 30 people, within South Korea's sovereign AI program.

Meta launched Muse Image, the first image generation model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, integrated into Meta AI, Instagram, and WhatsApp. The model uses multi-step reasoning, in conjunction with Muse Spark, to combine visual references and real-time web context in image composition.

MiniMax launched H3, a multimodal generative model that unifies text, image, video, and audio, producing 4 to 15-second videos in 2K with integrated native stereo audio. The company announced plans to publicly release the model's weights in the following days.

Meta Superintelligence Labs launched Muse Glimmer, a 30 billion parameter agentic model with open weights (Apache 2.0), optimized to run locally on a single consumer GPU (Mac or PC). The model targets local and always-on agent workflows, differentiating itself from cloud frontier models by running on personal hardware.

GLM-5.3 is a 743 billion parameter open model from Zhipu AI (Z.ai), which repurposes the GLM-5.2 base and concentrates gains in scaled post-training, achieving what the company describes as the strongest open-weight system in coding ever measured by them. The model also showed relevant emergent capability in offensive security, identifying 2,436 vulnerabilities in 269 projects during testing; weights will be released publicly in about two weeks.

Qwen3.8-27B is a 27.78 billion parameter dense multimodal (text, image, and video) model, with a native 262K token context, released under the Apache 2.0 license. It is the successor to Qwen3.6-27B and brings distilled capabilities from Qwen3.8-Max to a single local GPU model.

DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 is the general availability (GA) version of the DeepSeek V4 Pro flagship foundation model, with relevant improvements in agent capabilities in production environments and support for reasoning effort levels (low/high/max). The launch came with a change in API pricing policy, with differentiated peak and off-peak rates starting August 16, 2026.

GPT-5.6-Cyber is a model derived from GPT-5.6 Sol, specifically trained for offensive cybersecurity tasks, such as zero-day vulnerability discovery and exploit chain construction. It is the first OpenAI model to reach the 'High' level of cyber capability under its Preparedness Framework, distributed only to approved partners via the Daybreak Red program.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is an open Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 30 billion total parameters and 3 billion active, aimed at the high-volume execution layer for always-on agents. NVIDIA claims up to 4x faster output speed and 30% faster task completion than comparable models, capable of running on a single GPU.

Grok 4.6 is xAI's new foundation model, successor to Grok 4.5, aimed at long-duration agents, coding, and knowledge tasks, with a 500 thousand token context window. The model scored 61 points on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, tying with GPT-5.6 Sol at the maximum reasoning level.

Gemini 3.7 Flash is Google's new 'workhorse' model for coding and agents, with relevant gains in debugging and generating production-ready code over Gemini 3.6 Flash. It was launched with a promotional price at half the per-token cost of the previous model, valid until December 2026.

Open-weight multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model, with 125B total parameters (6B active) plus an additional N-gram embedding layer with 51B parameters, serving as a preview of the new Qwen4 architecture. Training with about 1/9 of the computational cost of Qwen3.7-Plus.

First natively multimodal model of the GLM-5 series, with a hybrid architecture combining sparse attention and linear attention, 320B total parameters (18B active) and a 1M token context window. Released under the MIT license, with performance close to GLM-5.3 at a tenth of the cost.

Successor to GPT-5.6 Sol, and the first OpenAI model to reach the 'Critical' level of cyber capability in the company's Preparedness Framework. It has a 1.05 million token context window and focuses on computer use, navigation, software engineering, and multi-step work, with a staggered launch for selected organizations, ChatGPT subscribers, and via API/AWS.

Third update of the Gemini 3 family's Flash line in six weeks, with improvements in software engineering, agentic tasks, and multi-step reasoning in specialized domains like finance and law. Maintains context of up to 1 million tokens and introductory pricing equal to version 3.7 Flash. Announced alongside Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber.

Cybersecurity-specialized variant of Gemini 3.8 Flash, focused on autonomous vulnerability discovery and automated patch generation, with restricted access for trusted testers via the Fairwind Program. Reports top-tier performance on pentest benchmarks at a lower cost than larger models. Announced alongside Gemini 3.8 Flash.

Update to Meta's closed reasoning model for coding and long-duration agents, with about 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than version 1.2 on comparable tasks. Meta reports a score of 75.4 on the DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark, surpassing Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on that test.

Google launched Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash in general availability via Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and Google Flow, extending the maximum duration of generated videos from 10 to 40 seconds through 10-second block extensions, with analysis of up to ten seconds of existing material to maintain consistency. The model adds first/last frame control, 360p draft mode, and export up to 4K.
